study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Mao et al., Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience, 2025
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Mapping early corpus callosum development to identify neurodevelopmental risk

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape (GAMLSS) to construct sex-specific growth curve models for corpus callosum morphometrics. The authors used a second-order polynomial function of age to avoid overfitting. The Box-Cox t (BCT) distribution was selected as the optimal model based on AIC and BIC criteria. Bootstrap resampling (1000 resamples) was employed to estimate 95% confidence intervals for the median growth curves.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Our modeling approach followed the method established by the World Health Organization (WHO) for constructing height/weight growth curves and utilized Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape (GAMLSS)... While nonlinear growth patterns were anticipated, we opted for a second-order polynomial function of age to avoid overfitting

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study extracted 10 morphological characteristics of the corpus callosum: (1) Total volume, (2) Anterior subregion volume, (3) Mid-anterior subregion volume, (4) Central subregion volume, (5) Mid-posterior subregion volume, (6) Posterior subregion volume, (7) Midsagittal plane area, (8) Midsagittal plane length, (9) Midsagittal plane perimeter, (10) Midsagittal plane circularity. Volume metrics were derived using FreeSurfer segmentation, and midsagittal morphological characteristics were obtained using Yuki software.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: To comprehensively describe the development of the corpus callosum, we extracted 10 morphological characteristics of the corpus callosum, including four morphological characteristics of the midsagittal plane (area, length, perimeter, circularity) and six volume-related characteristics (total volume, anterior, mid-anterior, central, mid-posterior, posterior).

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative models were constructed separately for each sex (sex-specific models). Age was modeled using a second-order polynomial function (including both linear and quadratic age terms). The models characterized age- and sex-dependent changes in corpus callosum morphometry.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We constructed sex-specific growth curve models for each corpus callosum morphological characteristic to address widely discussed sex differences in development... While nonlinear growth patterns were anticipated, we opted for a second-order polynomial function of age to avoid overfitting
